R316.note: ProcessBuilder with separate args plus hostname allowlist regex closes both shell and argument injection; no other behavior change.

R317.note: Per-category method allowlist blocks arbitrary dispatch while the one legitimate action (email.send) still resolves and dispatches normally.

R318.note: HtmlEncoder.Default.Encode applied to both interpolated values closes the reflected XSS; encoding is transparent for normal text (write-up mislabels the encoded snippet under '## Source' but the actual fix and explanation are correct).

R319.note: mathjs.evaluate() is the standard safe replacement for eval-based expression evaluation; preserves arithmetic semantics and adds error handling.

R320.note: Verified by compiling against EF Core 8: DbSet<T>.FromSql(FormattableString) exists and auto-parameterizes interpolated values; query semantics (tenant filter, LIKE pattern, async list) preserved per contract.

R321.note: th:utext to th:text is the correct minimal fix; output remains readable text, just escaped.

R322.note: Named-placeholder replacements option is standard Sequelize parameterization; query logic and response shape unchanged.

R323.note: StackExchange.Redis HashSet with HashEntry array uses RESP-level argument passing, correctly preventing CRLF command injection; constructor/type change is fully shown in the fix, and the resulting HSET semantics match the original two fields.

R324.note: RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes is the appropriate CSPRNG API; dropping the attacker-controlled seed is the correct behavior since a token generator should never accept caller-supplied entropy, and this is stated openly.

R325.note: Fixed loadProjectExport calls db.query(...) but `db` is never imported or defined anywhere in the file/module, so the function throws a ReferenceError on every invocation as written -- breaks all callers (owners included), not just attackers, and this is not flagged as non-functional/incomplete.

R326.note: self.get_object() restores DRF's queryset scoping and check_object_permissions, matching the stated contract (owner access, staff access, indistinguishable 404s) exactly.

R327.note: Saves node->next before free() and advances via the saved pointer; matches contract precisely, no other change.

R328.note: Pillow-based content verification plus UUID filenames and extension-from-content-type correctly closes CWE-434, but moving storage outside webroot (static/uploads -> uploads) removes the app's only way to serve the saved avatar, and the write-up only vaguely gestures at needing 'a handler that enforces access control' without stating that avatar retrieval is now broken until one is built.

R329.note: Passes the real allocated capacity (requestedCapacity) instead of the stale constant into write_field's bounds check; matches the stated contract exactly with a minimal one-line change.

R330.note: Jakarta Mail Session/Transport plus strict InternetAddress validation is the appropriate replacement for the raw-socket SMTP protocol and closes the CRLF injection; however it silently adds mail.smtp.starttls.required=true, which was absent from the original plain-port-25 flow and could make previously-successful sends fail against a server without STARTTLS, and this risk isn't called out.

R331.note: Adds secure=True (the reported finding) plus samesite='Lax'; consistent with the CWE's own HTTPS-session premise, and the write-up openly notes the HTTPS-enforcement assumption.

R332.note: Loops Stream.Read until the full 8-byte header is filled or EOF, rejecting short files before the signature check; preserves acceptance of valid PNG/PDF files unchanged.

R333.note: Extension allowlist (plus MIME check) correctly replaces the bypassable denylist for the reported extension-injection vector, but narrows accepted uploads from 'anything except .exe/.php/.sh/.bat' down to 8 office/image types without flagging that this will reject other previously-accepted attachment types the generic /attachments endpoint implies it should support.

R334.note: Inserting '--' before the filenames makes tar treat all subsequent arguments as literal positional filenames, exactly matching the stated contract's 'pass through as literal filename' option, with no other behavior change.
